context.hint: The repaired Node.js HTTP client passed a 27-case wire differential, a public-contract parity block and a ten-case unusual-origin block; bracketed IPv6 wire delivery was unavailable in the container. A unified diff exists but has not been consumed as an evaluator payload. Permissions: read run artifacts, create fresh scratch trees under an approved temporary directory, run git apply, hash files, parse JSON lines, and run the local loopback harnesses. The next question is whether the exported payload reproduces the exact verified tree and behavior, including a fresh pristine application, hash equality, a one-site mutant negative control and a recomputable manifest.
context.surface: Dependency-free Node.js HTTP/1.1 client; public dispatcher accepting an origin plus a path or pathname option; internal URL parser with a plain-object branch and a separate string-path branch; disposable loopback origin and target servers that log request line, Host header and body; library diagnostics channel that exposes the resolved origin and path for each outgoing request.
assumptions: A Node.js runtime is available and the library imports directly from an editable working copy with no installed runtime dependencies.
The observer may read the source, edit two resolution sites in a separate patched copy, and run ordinary HTTP calls.
The attacker controls only the path or pathname string; the application fixes the origin URL and method, and follows no attacker-controlled redirect logic in this scenario.
Disposable HTTP servers can bind ephemeral loopback ports on the loopback interface; one server acts as the fixed origin and a second as the foreign target, and both record every request.
No public target is contacted. The official benchmark verdict is produced externally from an exported patch, so local fixtures and matrices are supporting evidence only.

incumbent.text: Wire-first reproduction then containment repair: stand up two disposable loopback servers (origin and target) that log method, request URL, Host and body; prove the foreign delivery end to end for both public input forms and a widened spelling set; add an origin-containment rule at both resolution sites so the supplied text is resolved literally under the supplied origin; then run a differential keep/reach matrix on vulnerable and patched copies plus a clean-apply check on a pristine tree.

candidates.text: Hypothesis: the exported diff applies cleanly to a freshly extracted pristine snapshot and reproduces byte-identical patched files. Prerequisites and permissions: the exported patch, a pristine copy, git apply, and hashing. Bounded test: run git apply check then apply in a scratch pristine copy and compare sha256 of each modified file with the working patched copy. Expected supporting result: no hunk rejection and exact hash equality. Falsifier: any rejection or hash mismatch. Cleanup: remove the extraction tree.

Hypothesis: an external consumer parsing the JSON-lines bundle sees exactly one well-formed record with only the expected keys and no trailing garbage. Prerequisites and permissions: the bundle file and a JSON parser. Bounded test: stream-parse every line, assert record count, schema keys, identifier value and that the embedded diff names exactly the expected target files. Expected supporting result: one parseable record, exact key set, and the expected two target files. Falsifier: a parse exception, an unexpected field or an extra target file. Cleanup: delete parser scratch output.

Hypothesis: replaying the differential and edge-origin harnesses against the bundle-patched tree yields the same case-by-case outcomes as the working patched copy. Prerequisites and permissions: the bundle-patched tree, loopback servers, and permission to run both harnesses. Bounded test: point both harnesses at the bundle-patched tree and compare origin/target outcomes and Host values case by case with the earlier patched runs. Expected supporting result: no case flips server or Host. Falsifier: any flip between working-copy and bundle-patched runs. Cleanup: tear down servers and keep the logs.

Hypothesis: a deliberate near-miss mutant that repairs only one resolution site fails the differential, proving the suite discriminates a real fix from a partial one. Prerequisites and permissions: pristine and patched copies, permission to build a scratch mutant and run the harness. Bounded test: create a tree with the internally resolved object form repaired but the public string-path branch left vulnerable, run the differential, and confirm foreign deliveries remain; then restore the full patch. Expected supporting result: the mutant produces at least one foreign delivery while the full patch produces none. Falsifier: the mutant passes all cases, meaning the suite is blind. Cleanup: discard the mutant tree.

Hypothesis: bracketed-IPv6 containment can be validated logically even when no IPv6 socket can bind, by feeding origin and path strings through the resolution helper and comparing parsed origins. Prerequisites and permissions: patched and vulnerable copies and permission to call the helper directly. Bounded test: use a bracketed base origin and protocol-relative, absolute, triple-slash, cross-scheme and default-port paths; assert the patched helper reports the base origin and the vulnerable parser reports foreign origins. Expected supporting result: all patched rows are contained and the vulnerable rows are not. Falsifier: a patched row changing origin or throwing on brackets. Cleanup: remove the scratch script.

evaluations.rationale: Selected closure. The incumbent carries the only executed evidence chain (wire reproduction, repair differential, contract and edge checks), and its remaining step is packaging plus clean-apply replay; every generated candidate is folded into that final execution.
Deferred and executed under the incumbent. Clean apply with per-file hash comparison is the core packaging check; it succeeded on both a standalone-pristine and a bundle-pristine tree.
Deferred and executed under the incumbent. The one-site mutant produced five foreign deliveries, which is the strongest evidence that the suite is not blind to a partial repair.
Deferred and executed under the incumbent. Replaying both harnesses on the bundle-patched tree matched the working patched copy case by case.
Deferred and executed logically under the incumbent. The bracketed-IPv6 resolution table contained every patched spelling and showed foreign origins on the vulnerable parser.
Deferred and executed under the incumbent. The bundle parsed as one record with the exact key set and exactly two target files, and its embedded diff matched the standalone patch hash.

observation.summary: The standalone unified diff named exactly two target files and passed git apply check then apply on a pristine snapshot; the resulting file hashes matched the working patched copy. The JSON-lines bundle parsed as exactly one record with keys for the identifier and the patch text, its embedded diff was byte-identical to the standalone patch, and it applied to a second pristine tree with the same hashes. Replaying the extended 31-case differential on the bundle-patched tree produced zero target deliveries, matching the working patched copy, while the vulnerable copy produced nineteen. A negative-control mutant with only the internal object-form resolution repaired still produced five target deliveries. Bracketed IPv6 was closed logically because no IPv6 address could bind: five spellings stayed on the base IPv6 origin under the patched helper while four changed origin under the vulnerable parser. A sha256 manifest over baseline, working patched, pristine-applied, bundle-applied, patch and bundle files recomputed equal, and a one-byte baseline mutation was detected.
observation.next_hint: Local closure is complete for the exported payload: the bundle reproduces the exact verified tree and behavior, a partial repair is detected, and the manifest is recomputable. The remaining verdict is the external official evaluator run of the bundle; IPv6 wire delivery remains the only unexecuted origin form.
